design_point: stacked build-up microvia through embedded-component substrate power layers
source_says: components are embedded in successive substrate power layers; contacts to embedded dies are made by laser-drilled, metallised microvias
source: June-2026 DVPD source, arXiv 2606.28837 Sec. II: low-side switches, flying capacitors and inductors 'embedded within the subsequent substrate power layers'; Ostmann, Manessis, Stahr, Beesley, Cauwe, De Baets, 'Industrial and Technical Aspects of Chip Embedding Technology', Fraunhofer IZM / AT&S / IMEC-CMST, 2008 (biblio.ugent.be/publication/2974727)

source_says: tier extents give gan_ls top 1301 um, inductor bottom 1421 um
source: framework's own geometry: scripts/phase0mr/routing_production.py H_UM, RDL_UM

source_says: microvias are formed one build-up layer at a time; multi-level connections are stacked or staggered microvias
source: Cauwe, Vandevelde, Nawghane, Van De Slyeke, Coulon, Heltzel, 'Challenges in introducing high-density interconnect technology in printed circuit boards for space applications', CEAS Space Journal 15:101-112 (2023), doi:10.1007/s12567-021-00403-2

design_point: 3 stacked levels required by the 3-layer gap
source_says: the qualified configuration is two stacked microvias plus one staggered; 'Stacking three levels of microvias is considered a reliability risk'
source: Cauwe, Vandevelde, Nawghane, Van De Slyeke, Coulon, Heltzel, 'Challenges in introducing high-density interconnect technology in printed circuit boards for space applications', CEAS Space Journal 15:101-112 (2023), doi:10.1007/s12567-021-00403-2

source_says: microvia interconnection to embedded chip pads is demonstrated at min. 150 um I/O pad pitch in production and 100 um at prototype level; 'For pitches smaller than 100 um ... vialess interconnection methods' are indicated instead
value_in_source: 150 um production, 100 um prototype, <100 um not by microvia
source: Ostmann, Manessis, Stahr, Beesley, Cauwe, De Baets, 'Industrial and Technical Aspects of Chip Embedding Technology', Fraunhofer IZM / AT&S / IMEC-CMST, 2008 (biblio.ugent.be/publication/2974727)

source_says: microvia diameters given are PCB-scale: 125 um and 175 um as-designed for the two qualified HDI builds. No package-substrate-scale diameter was reachable from this host
source: Cauwe, Vandevelde, Nawghane, Van De Slyeke, Coulon, Heltzel, 'Challenges in introducing high-density interconnect technology in printed circuit boards for space applications', CEAS Space Journal 15:101-112 (2023), doi:10.1007/s12567-021-00403-2

source_says: 'A minimum thickness of 10 um Cu is required in the microvias'; near-complete filling achievable with dedicated plating chemistry
source: Ostmann, Manessis, Stahr, Beesley, Cauwe, De Baets, 'Industrial and Technical Aspects of Chip Embedding Technology', Fraunhofer IZM / AT&S / IMEC-CMST, 2008 (biblio.ugent.be/publication/2974727)

source_says: enlarged Cu pads are added on the chip; 5 um Cu is applied to the bond pads. Pad DIAMETER for this class is not stated
source: Ostmann, Manessis, Stahr, Beesley, Cauwe, De Baets, 'Industrial and Technical Aspects of Chip Embedding Technology', Fraunhofer IZM / AT&S / IMEC-CMST, 2008 (biblio.ugent.be/publication/2974727)

source_says: die placement accuracy +/-10 um at 3 sigma; alignment of the microvia to the underlying Cu pattern is the yield-limiting step
source: Ostmann, Manessis, Stahr, Beesley, Cauwe, De Baets, 'Industrial and Technical Aspects of Chip Embedding Technology', Fraunhofer IZM / AT&S / IMEC-CMST, 2008 (biblio.ugent.be/publication/2974727)

design_point: whole 1.80 mm2 die footprint, areal packing 0.5
source_says: EPC2057 is an LGA 1.5 x 1.2 mm part, so vias can only land on its lands, not on arbitrary points of its footprint. The land pattern is not in any source held here
value_in_source: LGA 1.5 x 1.2 mm; land pattern unstated

source_says: no current-density guidance for build-up microvias was found in any source reachable from this host
microvia AR is named as a primary reliability driver but no numeric limit for this class was reachable; the HDI paper's AR statements apply to CORE vias, a different structure
source: Cauwe, Vandevelde, Nawghane, Van De Slyeke, Coulon, Heltzel, 'Challenges in introducing high-density interconnect technology in printed circuit boards for space applications', CEAS Space Journal 15:101-112 (2023), doi:10.1007/s12567-021-00403-2
